capture: CDP runtime probe of https://www.sejda.com/pdf-editor in headless Chrome 155.0.8059.85 (Windows), 2026-10-24
method: Uploaded D:\small_editor\samples\sample.pdf through input.fileupload; opened the Text tool group caret; clicked 'Find & Replace'; drove #findText, #replaceText, #replaceMatchCase, .btn-find-next, .btn-replace-find-next with native value setters and real clicks.
intervention: The Find & Replace menu item is hidden until a document is loaded; a document was uploaded to make it reachable. No application code was modified.
document_fixture: 4-page A4 PDF generated by scripts/make-sample.mjs; page 1 contains 'merge' twice on one line, 'Merge PDF files...' on another line and 'Merge is not merge.' on a third line.

observations.sequence: query merge, Match case unchecked, Find
observations.note: 3 = number of matching text lines, not occurrences (page 1 has 5 case-insensitive occurrences).
Page 2 has 'merge merge merge' on one line; still counted as 1.
Cycling walks page order and wraps.
Unchecked = case-insensitive (merge and Merge both 3). Checked = case-sensitive (lowercase-only and uppercase-only each 2). 'the' matches 3 lines, again per line.

observations.result: Exactly one .find-replace-highlight element, positioned over the matched line (left 70.76px, width 284.6px, font-size 15.33px). Only the current hit is outlined.

observations.dom_after: The matched line rendered 'Find the word REPLACED on this page: REPLACED.' — every occurrence inside that text line was replaced.
observations.note: Replace appears to operate on the matched text line/run, not on a single occurrence.

unresolved: The implementation is inside /js/pages/pdf-editor.min.obfuscated.js (394,992 bytes); searching that file for 'searchStatus', 'findText', 'replaceMatchCase', 'searchReplaceTextPrompt' and 'btn-replace-all' returned no matches, so the exact algorithm could not be read statically.

After a sequence that included empty and whitespace-only queries plus regex metacharacters, the page stopped responding to Runtime.evaluate within 120s; behaviour for empty/regex queries is therefore unknown, not 'broken'.
Behaviour for 'Include links' was not exercised (the fixture has no link annotations).
